config.physim.autoOpenOnSimulate.descrip: Auto-open the panel when a script is run.
config.physim.panel.openLocation.descrip: Where to place the Physics Sensor panel when it opens.
config.physim.panel.openLocation.enumDes: Open the panel beside the active editor in the current window (default).
Open the panel in a new floating window (requires VSCode 1.85+).
config.physim.monitors.openInNewWindow.m: Show the microcontroller's monitors in a separate window instead of below the 3D view. The window opens with the first monitor of each run; closing it puts the monitors back into the panel until the next run. `PhySim: Open Monitors in New Window` opens it on demand.
config.physim.keybindings.useF6F7.markdo: Bind F6 to `PhySim: Run` and F7 to `PhySim: Build` in Lua editors. Turn this off when *Stormworks Lua with LifeBoatAPI* is installed too and you want F6 / F7 to stay with it. Shift+F6 (run) and Shift+F7 (build) work either way.
config.physim.agent.showInPanel.markdown: Show what an AI agent runs through PhySim's MCP server (beta) in this window's panel: the monitors and the pose, updated after each of the agent's tool calls. The window only watches; it cannot change the agent's run. It listens on a local socket (a named pipe on Windows) named after the workspace folder, not on a network port. Turn this off to stop listening.
config.physim.libraryPaths.markdownDescr:
Extra folders `require` searches, after the workspace folder and in the order listed. Relative paths are taken from the workspace folder.

`require("a.b")` looks for `a/b.lua`, then `a/b/init.lua`, in each folder.
config.physim.build.minify.description: Minify when building. When off, the build only links `require`d files and removes simulator-only parts, leaving the output readable.
config.physim.build.outputDirectory.desc: Folder the built Lua is written to. A relative path is taken from the workspace folder.
debug.program.description: The microcontroller's Lua file to run. When omitted, the file in the active editor is run.
debug.snippet.description: Run the Lua file in the active editor with PhySim.
